Objective truth, on the other hand, is independent of personal feelings or opinions. It is based on facts and evidence that can be consistently observed and verified by others. To distinguish between the two, one can employ critical thinking and seek evidence. Peer review and replication of results are also key in establishing objective truths, as they help ensure that findings are not merely the result of individual biases or errors.
